whatis.h2: What is the breakeven on a price change?
whatis.intro: The breakeven on a price change is how much volume you can lose after a raise before profit drops below today's. After a cut, it is how much volume you must add. It compares contribution per case before and after the move.

cards.title: The truck still stops
cards.body: The breakeven treats the $22.00 product cost as your only cost per case. Lose cases at an account and the truck still stops there, so each remaining case costs more to deliver.
cards.alt: Delivery truck, for delivery costs that a lost case does not remove

cards.title: Lost volume can hide in the mix
cards.body: An account can answer a raise by switching to a cheaper line you also carry. Its total cases hold steady, so the loss hides unless you check the item itself.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for volume that trades down to a cheaper line

cards.title: Contract accounts sit outside it
cards.body: An account on a fixed price term or a cost-plus contract cannot take a 5% list move mid-term. Run the breakeven on the volume you can actually reprice.
cards.alt: Minus sign, for contract accounts a list price move does not reach

who.intro: Before a distributor moves a price, someone has to say how much volume the change can survive. Anyone who defends a raise or signs off on a cut should know the volume line first.

look.h2: Get the inputs right before you read the breakeven
look.intro: The ratio itself is exact. The inputs behind it are where a price decision goes wrong, usually in one of these three.

steps.title: A cost per case that is current
steps.body: Enter what the case costs you today, freight in, not last quarter's invoice. An old cost makes the contribution look bigger or smaller than it really is.

steps.title: The price accounts actually pay
steps.body: Start from the net price after rebates, deals and contract discounts, not the list. A raise worked off a list price nobody pays tells you very little.

steps.title: A month that is typical
steps.body: The monthly dollars use the case count you type in. Take it from a normal month, not a holiday peak or a slow stretch, or the swing reads wrong.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits after a price move
vos.body: VOS does not set prices or work out the breakeven. It helps with the check that comes after. Orders from the VOS app build each account's order history, which you see in one admin platform.
bullets: Order history per account, to check volume after a move
Each account's guide carries the prices you set
Each app order has a number, date and timestamp
Most distributors are live in 24 to 48 hours
